spots.name: Golden Hill Jewish Cemetery
spots.summary: Golden Hill Cemetery is located at 5025 North 42nd Street in the North Omaha neighborhood of Omaha, Nebraska.

spots.name: Mutual of Omaha Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mutual of Omaha Headquarters Tower is a 44-story office skyscraper under construction in Downtown Omaha, Nebraska, United States.

spots.name: Omaha's Henry Doorly Zoo and Aquarium
spots.summary: Omaha's Henry Doorly Zoo and Aquarium is a zoo in Omaha, Nebraska. It is accredited by the Association of Zoos and Aquariums and a member of the World Association of Zoos and Aquariums.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Omaha's Henry Doorly Zoo and Aquarium

spots.name: WoodmenLife Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The WoodmenLife Tower is an office skyscraper in Downtown Omaha, Nebraska, United States, and headquarters of the insurance company WoodmenLife. Construction of the building began in 1966 and was completed in the spring of 1969.

spots.name: Joslyn Art Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Wed, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Joslyn Art Museum, commonly referred to as the Joslyn, is a fine arts museum in Omaha, Nebraska, the largest in the state. It opened in 1931 at the initiative of Sarah H. Joslyn, in memory of her husband, businessman George A. Joslyn.

spots.name: Bob Kerrey Pedestrian Bridge
spots.summary: The Bob Kerrey Pedestrian Bridge, also called Bob the Bridge, is a footbridge across the Missouri River between Omaha, Nebraska and Council Bluffs, Iowa. It opened in 2008, and is named after former Nebraska Senator Bob Kerrey, who secured federal funding for the bridge.

spots.name: Durham Museum

hours.note: Closed Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Durham Museum is located at 801 South 10th Street in Downtown Omaha, Nebraska, United States. The museum is dedicated to preserving and displaying the history of the United States' western region. The museum is housed in Omaha's former Union Station.

photo.author: Tony Webster from Minneapolis, Minnesota, United States

spots.name: Gene Leahy Mall
spots.summary: Gene Leahy Mall, also known locally as The Mall, is a 9.6-acre (39,000 m2) park located in Downtown Omaha, Nebraska, United States. The park features two large slides, a sculpture garden, a remote-control boat cove, a large children's play area, and an amphitheater where outdoor concerts are held in the summer.

spots.name: St. John's Parish

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. John's Parish is a Roman Catholic church located at 2500 California Plaza on the Creighton University campus in Omaha, Nebraska, United States. It is within the Archdiocese of Omaha and is a ministry of the Midwest Province of the Society of Jesus (Jesuits).

spots.name: Kountze Memorial Lutheran Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Kountze Memorial Lutheran Church is located at 2650 Farnam Street in Midtown Omaha, Nebraska. Organized on December 5, 1858, as Emanuel's Evangelical Lutheran Church, the church is thought to be the first Lutheran congregation organized west of the Missouri River.

spots.name: Omaha National Bank Building
spots.summary: The Omaha National Bank Building was built in 1888–89 at 1650 Farnam Street in Downtown Omaha, Nebraska. Designed by McKim, Mead & White in the Italian Renaissance style, the building was saved from demolition by a rehabilitation in 1978.

photo.author: Original uploader was JonClee86 at en.wikipedia

spots.name: J. L. Brandeis and Sons Store Building
spots.summary: The J. L. Brandeis and Sons Store Building is located at 210 South 16th Street in the central business district of Omaha, Nebraska. Formerly the headquarters location of the Brandeis Department Store chain, it currently holds apartments and condominiums known as The Brandeis.
spots.wikipediaTitle: J. L. Brandeis and Sons Store Building

spots.name: Douglas County Courthouse
spots.summary: The Douglas County Courthouse is a county courthouse located at 1701 Farnam Street in Omaha, Nebraska, United States. Built in 1912, it was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1979. Notable events at the courthouse include two lynchings and the city's first sit-in during the Civil Rights Movement.

photo.author: Tony Webster from Minneapolis, Minnesota, United States (c) 2018 Tony Webster to

spots.name: Omaha Rail and Commerce Historic District
spots.summary: The Omaha Rail and Commerce Historic District, roughly bounded by Jackson, 15th, and 8th Streets, as well as the Union Pacific main line, is located in downtown Omaha, Nebraska.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Omaha Rail and Commerce Historic District

spots.name: First National Bank Building
spots.summary: The First National Bank Building is a U-shaped, fourteen-story, historic steel structure building located on the corner of 16th and Farnam street in Downtown Omaha, Nebraska. The building was constructed in 1917.

spots.name: Hupmobile Building
spots.summary: The Hupmobile Building is located at 2523 Farnam Street in Midtown Omaha, Nebraska. Built in 1917 on the city's historic Auto Row, the building was an early Hupmobile dealership. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2014.

spots.name: Farnam Building
spots.summary: The Farnam Building is located in Downtown Omaha, Nebraska. It is a seven-story, 110-foot-tall (34 m), historic building that was constructed in 1929. It is adjacent to the First National Bank Building to the east, and Farnam Plaza, an eight-story building that houses the Opera Omaha offices, to the west.

photo.author: JonClee86. Original uploader was JonClee86 at en.wikipedia

spots.name: Omaha Central Library
spots.summary: Omaha Central Library is a public library in Omaha, Nebraska, United States. It is the main branch of the Omaha Public Library system. The four-story library was designed by Omaha-based HDR, Inc. and Alley Poyner Marchietto. Omaha Central Library features local artwork around the building.

spots.name: Nash Block
spots.summary: Nash Block, historically known as the McKesson-Robbins Warehouse, is a historic building located at 902-912 Farnam Street in Omaha, Nebraska. Designed by Thomas R. Kimball and built from 1905 to 1907, the building is the last remnant of Downtown Omaha's Jobbers Canyon.

spots.name: Christian Specht Building
spots.summary: The Christian Specht Building is located at 1110 Douglas Street in Downtown Omaha, Nebraska, United States. It is the only existing building with a cast-iron facade known in Nebraska today, and one of the few ever built in the state.

spots.name: Charles Schwab Field
spots.summary: Charles Schwab Field Omaha is a ballpark in Omaha, Nebraska, United States. Opened in 2011, the city-owned stadium replaced the historic Johnny Rosenblatt Stadium, which was about two miles (3 km) south. The diamond is aligned southeast at an approximate elevation of 1,010 feet (310 m) above sea level.

spots.name: Do Space

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Do Space is a 501(c)(3) non-profit community technology center in Omaha, Nebraska, United States. The center's services include a digital library, an educational center, and small makerspace featuring 3D printing technology. The library opened in 2015.

spots.name: Poppleton Block
spots.summary: The Poppleton Block is located at 1001 Farnam Street in Downtown Omaha, Nebraska. The building was built in 1880 for Omaha lawyer and politician A.J. Poppleton, and was designated an Omaha Landmark on July 13, 1982, and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places later that year.

spots.name: Barker Building
spots.summary: The Barker Building, a seven-story apartment building located at 306 South 15th Street in Downtown Omaha, Nebraska, United States. Built in 1929, it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on July 2, 2008.

spots.name: Scottish Rite Cathedral
spots.summary: The Scottish Rite Cathedral is a Masonic building in Omaha in the state of Nebraska in the Midwestern United States. Begun in 1912 and opened in 1914, it remains in use by the Scottish Rite.

spots.name: V. Mertz

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: An intimate and romantic ambiance residing in the Old Market. The menu, which changes weekly, is continental but also offers some innovative culinary creations from a range of cuisine types. Great for special dinners. Famous clientele have included Bono of U2, Warren Buffet, and Bruce Springsteen. Reservations only.

spots.name: Spencer's for Steaks and Chops

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Aged, hand cut and seared meats. Featuring USDA prime beef from Stockyards Beef of Chicago, Spencer’s restaurant offers sizzling hot porterhouses, juicy filet mignon and the bone-in ribeye for which Spencer’s is named. Validated parking in the Hilton Garden Inn Garage. Reservations preferred.

spots.name: The Boiler Room

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Boiler Room is a hidden gem in the south side of the Old Market tucked in the gutted boiler room of an old warehouse. The food is usually sourced locally and has a heavy emphasis on gourmet French-style cooking, especially meat. Try the boar's head or scorpionfish. The menu changes daily.

spots.name: Hiro 88

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Hiro 88 is an upscale Pan-Asian restaurant group. With the help of renowned architects like Japan’s Nakamura-san, restaurateur Milton Yin has created distinct atmospheres at each location, each inspired by its surrounding neighborhood. Serving Chinese cuisine and some of Omaha’s best sushi.

spots.name: Blue Line Coffee

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Resides in a walkable area of Omaha, the Dundee neighborhood. Stop in and get "Green Beret", then walk down the block to 'Great Harvest' for a free slice of bread of your choice. Alternatively, walk west to the Bread Oven, a French bakery featuring traditional French breads.

spots.name: The Crescent Moon

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sat

spots.summary: A large pub with a German Bier Hall down below. Checkout Max and Joe's tasting room next door. If you find a drink you like, stop in Beertopia to grab a six-pack of it, or any other craft beer you'd like, both owned by the same people. A must visit for all lovers of beer.

spots.name: Upstream Brewery

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: In the Old Market. Has pool tables and on Wednesday nights $7 pizzas and $2 microbrews are served. Also has a full menu and great food at a reasonable price. Try the sample platter of microbrews and get your favorite in a growler to go.

spots.name: The Down Under Lounge

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Eclectic bar with unique, quality cocktails. Be prepared to wait a few minutes while the bartenders mix them. Free live music W-Sa. Diverse and agreeable crowd. Before 9PM, order take-out from Mother India just a block west.

spots.name: The Max
spots.summary: Ostensibly the region's largest dance club and gay bar. Two dance floors (electronica on one, hip-hop on the other), three bars, and a huge courtyard. On the weekends it's mostly straight people and expect a $5 cover.

spots.name: California Tacos and More

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Specializing in fried "puffy-shell" tacos, this small taco place offers filling Mexican food, quick and cheap. Tables get scarce in the afternoon. Happy hour is 4PM-5PM.

spots.name: 13th Street Coffee Company

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: In Downtown, it serves a variety of coffee-based drinks. Desserts and sandwiches are also served. Occasionally there is live music on Fridays. Free wi-fi.

spots.name: The Homy Inn
spots.summary: Champagne on tap. This cozy bar is decorated with collectibles and memorabilia from yesteryear. Friendly atmosphere and a relaxed place to kick back.

spots.name: 801 Chophouse

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: A white cloth dining establishment in downtown Omaha. Offers lobster, American Waygu, and single malt scotch. Reservations only. Chain Restaurant.

spots.name: Block 16

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Nationally recognized street food. A large menus featuring juicy burgers, fried chicken, and poutine. Alcoholic drinks available as well.

spots.name: Ahmad's Persian Cuisine

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Great, authentic Persian food. All meals are prepared by the restaurant's owner, Ahmad, an Iranian immigrant. Located in the Old Market.

spots.name: Los Portales
spots.summary: Authentic Mexican that caters to the more adventurous diners. Examples include steak served with cactus, quail, and tongue burritos.

spots.name: Dinker's Bar

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Since 1965, this bar and grill has been serving up high class burgers and beer. A great place to relax after a long day.

spots.name: El Pollo Tote

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: Offering breakfast and specializing in roasted chicken. An authentic Mexican experience.

spots.name: Avoli Osteria

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A Northern Italian restaurant, located in the historic Omaha neighborhood of Dundee.
